newsitem.title: USA: Pepco, RCN join to offer telecom services.
newsitem.headline: Pepco, RCN join to offer telecom services.

text.p: Potomac Electric Power Co and RCN Corp Wednesday said they will invest up to $300 million together to offer the Washington area local and long-distance phone service, cable television and access to the Internet.
A Pepco unit and RCN will own the joint venture equally. It will provide the telecommunications services over an advanced fiber-optic network.
Within three years, the new venture plans to offer more than 40 major communities the "bundled" services that include the first full-service alternative to current cable-TV firms.
RCN is a subsidiary of C-TEC Corp.
C-TEC said it has received approval from the Internal Revenue Service to spin off RCN into a separate, publicly traded company by the end of 1997. RCN is expected to trade on the Nasdaq stock market.
Initial network construction will begin in the District of Columbia and portions of Maryland and Northern Virginia.

In advance of the buildout of the fiber optic network, a "competitive package" of local and long-distance phone and Internet services will be offered throughout the Washington area, the companies said.
The move by Pepco into the telecommunications business follows enactment of last year's telecom law, which allows the phone, cable-TV and utility industries to invade each other's business.

"By becoming an integrated provider of energy and telecommunications services in the Washington metropolitan area, Pepco will be better able to successfully compete in a deregulated environment," Pepco President John Derrick said.
RCN currently provides bundled telecommunications services in New York City and, in concert with Boston Edison Co, in the Boston metropolitan area.
